plan.summary: This 4-week block fits an off-camp 12-week boxing plan with a build-first emphasis. With only 1 S&C session per week, the goal is to keep quality high and fatigue controlled so sparring stays the priority. Week 1 establishes simple performance baselines with bodyweight strength tests and jump output, then Weeks 2-3 build full-body strength and power using safe bodyweight movements, and Week 4 deloads by cutting volume while keeping speed and crisp technique.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build full-body strength and basic power with low-equipment work that supports boxing without adding unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress bodyweight strength and explosive intent while keeping the weekly session compact and recoverable around boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and express it faster through sharper jumps, throws if equipment improves, and low-fatigue speed work.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quick dip and controlled landing. Stop each rep if height drops off.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best jump set for height and sharpness.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement jump feels uncoordinated. Start from a still quarter squat and jump fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box if landing on the floor bothers your joints. Step down between reps.

exercises.name: Push-Up Test Set
exercises.notes: Use strict form and stop before the last ugly rep. This establishes your current pressing baseline for the next block.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log total clean reps from this set so future progress is easy to compare.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up Test Set
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, box, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are not yet clean.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lower and stand up hard. Keep torso tall and front foot flat.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats feel awkward. Step back softly and keep balance steady.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable step or bench if available. Drive through the whole foot.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Pull chest toward the bar or table edge with a straight body. Stop each set before body position breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a sturdy setup and keep the angle manageable. Prioritize safety and smooth reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: If no row setup exists, pull hard against a secure anchor for 15-20 second efforts.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel and finish with the glute, not the low back. Pause briefly at the top.

substitutionOptions.name: Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use both legs if the single-leg version causes cramping or loss of control.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Keep ribs down and low back lightly pressed toward the floor. Shorten the lever if position is lost.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow hold is too difficult. Move slowly and keep the trunk braced.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a hard full-body plank if you need a simpler option.

exercises.name: Front Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Use very light hand resistance and keep the neck long. This should feel easy and controlled, not max effort.

substitutionOptions.name: Supine Head Lift Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Lift the head slightly off the floor and hold if manual resistance is not practical.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump high, reset between reps, and land quietly. Keep every rep crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you do better with a simpler jump pattern.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low box and step down if floor landings feel rough.

exercises.name: 1a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a variation that leaves 1-2 clean reps in reserve. Drive up fast while keeping the body straight.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use the hardest variation you can do cleanly for all work sets and note the reps completed.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands if floor push-ups are still too hard to perform cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Kneeling Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if needed to keep full range and strong body position.

exercises.name: 1b. Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Pull with the upper back first and keep the ribs down. Make each rep smooth and controlled.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a safe sturdy setup and adjust the body angle to match your strength.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use 15-20 second hard pulls against a secure anchor if no row setup exists.

exercises.name: 2a. Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.notes: Sit down under control and stand up hard. Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the cleanest rep count and difficulty so you can progress range or variation over time.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rear-foot elevation is too unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a more natural stepping pattern.

exercises.name: 2b. Pike Push-Up
exercises.notes: Lower the head between the hands and press up smoothly. Keep the body stacked as much as possible.

substitutionOptions.name: Downward Dog Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a shorter range if shoulder strength is still developing.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Pike Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Elevate the hands to reduce the load and keep the pattern clean.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Pause at the top and keep the pelvis level. Do not twist through the trunk.

substitutionOptions.name: Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use both legs if the single-leg version loses control.

exercises.name: Leg Raise
exercises.notes: Move slowly and keep the lower back controlled. Bend the knees if needed to keep good position.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if straight-leg raises pull too much on the hips.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use timed holds if reps are too hard to control yet.

exercises.name: Side Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Use light hand resistance only. Keep the jaw relaxed and the posture tall.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Head Lift Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a floor-based hold if manual resistance is awkward.

exercises.name: Skater Jump
exercises.notes: Jump side to side with a soft stick on each landing. Cover only as much distance as you can control cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Lateral Bound to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a smaller distance and pause the landing if you need more control.

substitutionOptions.name: Line Hop
substitutionOptions.notes: Use quick low side-to-side hops if single-leg landings feel too advanced.

exercises.name: 1a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use the hardest clean variation you can repeat across all sets. Press fast and keep the trunk rigid.

performanceTarget.prompt: Try to beat Week 2 with either more reps or a harder variation while keeping form clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Decline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are now too easy and you can still keep strong position.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups still break down before the rep target.

exercises.name: 1b. Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Keep the body straight and squeeze the shoulder blades back at the top. Do not jerk into position.

performanceTarget.prompt: Aim to improve your body angle or reps while keeping the same clean standard.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Adjust the body angle so every rep stays smooth.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use 3-4 hard timed efforts if no row setup is available.

exercises.name: 2a. Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.notes: Control the drop and stand up aggressively. Keep your balance and full foot pressure on the front leg.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the rear-foot-elevated version is still unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if stepping feels smoother and safer.

exercises.name: 2b. Pike Push-Up
exercises.notes: Lower under control and press up strongly. Keep shoulders active and avoid collapsing into the neck.

substitutionOptions.name: Downward Dog Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a shorter range if the full version is still too demanding.

substitutionOptions.name: Wall Handstand Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a short hold if pressing reps are not yet controlled but you want overhead strength exposure.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Reach the free leg back and keep hips square. Move slowly enough to own the balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Hip Airplane Supported
substitutionOptions.notes: Use support from a wall or rack if balance is the main limiter.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if hinging on one leg is too unstable right now.

exercises.name: V-Up or Tuck-Up
exercises.notes: Move with control and keep the trunk braced. Use the tuck version if the full V-up is too loose.

substitutionOptions.name: Leg Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the V-up turns into a swinging movement.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler trunk flexion option.

exercises.name: Back Neck Isometric
exercises.notes: Use light hand resistance and hold a neutral head position. This is a brief easy dose, not a grind.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Head Lift Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Lift the forehead slightly from the floor and hold if manual resistance is not practical.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep the jumps fast and clean. Stop early if the pop is not there.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler explosive pattern this week.

exercises.name: 1a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use the same variation as recent weeks or slightly easier. Finish feeling fresh, not drained.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need an easier deload option with crisp reps.

exercises.name: 1b. Inverted Row
exercises.notes: Keep the reps smooth and leave more in the tank than usual. Focus on clean body position.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a comfortable angle and avoid grinding.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use short moderate efforts if no row setup is available.

exercises.name: 2a. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Move under control and keep the effort moderate. This week is for recovery and pattern quality.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels more natural and easier to recover from.

exercises.name: 2b. Pike Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a smooth range and stop well before form slips. Keep shoulders active.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Pike Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this easier version if needed to keep the deload truly light.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Pause briefly at the top and keep the ribs down. Easy quality reps only.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if the standard version feels very easy and still fresh.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Own the position and keep breathing calm. Short clean holds are enough this week.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the hollow shape is too hard to keep clean.
